proxy-ui-api.rate-limit-requests-per-second: Management REST API request rate limit per second. Rate limits apply per each requesting IP.
proxy-ui-api.rate-limit-requests-per-minute: Management REST API request rate limit per minute. Rate limits apply per each requesting IP.
proxy-ui-api.rate-limit-cache-size: Controls how many IP addresses can be remembered in the rate-limit cache Tradeoff between memory usage and protection from a large attack.
proxy-ui-api.rate-limit-expire-after-access-minutes: Controls how long the rate-limit cache entries are valid
proxy-ui-api.cache-default-ttl: Configures default cache expiration in seconds. Cache is hit during authentication requests. Setting the value to -1 disables the cache.
proxy-ui-api.cache-api-key-ttl: Configures Api Key cache expiration in seconds. Can be used by various api services. Setting the value to -1 disables the cache.
proxy-ui-api.strict-identifier-checks: Configures identifier input validation (member code, subsystem code etc). Values: true- identifiers must mach pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9'()+,-.=?]*. false- identfiers must not contain colon (:), semicolon (;), slashes (/\), percent (%) or control characters.
proxy-ui-api.request-size-limit-regular: Maximum size of Management REST API requests
proxy-ui-api.request-size-limit-binary-upload: Maximum size of Management REST API requests for file uploads
proxy-ui-api.authentication-key-algorithm: Key algorithm used for creating authentication certificate request. Possible values are RSA and EC. (since version 7.6)
proxy-ui-api.signing-key-algorithm: Key algorithm used for creating signing certificate request. Possible values are RSA and EC. (since version 7.6)
proxy-ui-api.authentication-provider: Authentication provider used for UI login. Possible values are PAM or DATABASE.
proxy-ui-api.enforce-user-password-policy: When enabled, user passwords must meet the configured password policy.
proxy-ui-api.auto-update-timestamp-service-url: If enabled, makes the security server update the timestamping service URLs when they are changed on the central server. In case there are multiple timestamping services with the same name, the update will not be done and a warning is logged instead.
proxy-ui-api.automatic-activate-auth-certificate: If enabled, authentication certificates are activated automatically after they have been registered on the Central Server.
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-success-notification-enable: If enabled, notification e-mail is sent to the member when automatic certificate renewal has successfully renewed a certificate
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-failure-notification-enable: If enabled, notification e-mail is sent to the member when automatic certificate renewal has failed to renew a certificate
proxy-ui-api.auth-cert-registered-notification-enable: If enabled, notification e-mail is sent to the member when authentication certificate has been registered in global configuration
proxy-ui-api.cert-auto-activation-notification-enable: If enabled, notification e-mail is sent to the member when automatic certificate activation was successful
proxy-ui-api.cert-auto-activation-failure-notificatio: If enabled, notification e-mail is sent to the member when automatic certificate activation has failed
proxy-ui-api.mail-notification-locale: Locale for mail notifications, which determines the language of the notifications.
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-active: If enabled, the ACME automatic certificate renewal job will run periodically
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-retry-delay: Amount of seconds between automatic ACME certificate renewal runs, if the last run was a failure
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-interval: Seconds between ACME renewal check cycles.
proxy-ui-api.acme-renewal-time-before-expiration-date: When to trigger next automatic renewal. Subtracted as days from the expiration date of the certificate. Used when it's not possible to receive the ACME renewal information from the ACME server.
proxy-ui-api.acme-keypair-renewal-time-before-expirat: When to trigger automatic ACME account keypair renewal subtracted as days from the expiration date of the certificate
proxy-ui-api.automatic-activate-acme-sign-certificate: If enabled, signing certificates are activated automatically when they have been ordered from via ACME (new or renew)
proxy-ui-api.acme-authorization-wait-attempts: Number of attempts to check whether the ACME authorizations have completed before giving up
proxy-ui-api.acme-authorization-wait-interval: Amount of time in milliseconds to wait between ACME authorization completion check attempts
proxy-ui-api.acme-certificate-wait-attempts: Number of attempts to poll for ACME certificate issuance.
proxy-ui-api.acme-certificate-wait-interval: Seconds between ACME certificate issuance polling attempts.
proxy-ui-api.acme-certificate-account-key-pair-expira: Amount of days the ACME server account's self-signed certificate is valid
proxy-ui-api.acme-challenge-port-enabled: If enabled, the API will listen on acme challenge port (default 80) for incoming ACME challenge requests
proxy-ui-api.acme-challenge-port: Custom port number for ACME challenges. When set, the Security Server host's port 80 needs to redirect to this port, because ACME Servers always use port 80 for the challenge.
proxy-ui-api.acme-key-length: RSA key length in bits used for ACME certificate requests.
proxy-ui-api.acme-account-keystore-path: File system path to the keystore holding the ACME account key pair.
proxy-ui-api.acme-challenge-path: File system path where ACME HTTP-01 challenge tokens are served.
proxy-ui-api.allow-csr-for-key-with-certificate: Controls if generating the new CSR is allowed for a key that has an existing certificate.
proxy-ui-api.auth-cert-reg-signature-digest-algorithm: Signature digest algorithm used for generating authentication certificate registration request. Possible values are - SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512.
proxy-ui-api.proxy-server-url: URL of the Security Server proxy used by the Admin API.
proxy-ui-api.proxy-server-connect-timeout: Milliseconds to wait when establishing a connection to the proxy server.
proxy-ui-api.proxy-server-socket-timeout: Milliseconds to wait for data from the proxy server socket (0 = no timeout).
proxy-ui-api.proxy-server-enable-connection-reuse: When enabled, HTTP connections to the proxy server are reused across requests.
proxy-ui-api.proxy-tls-protocols: TLS protocols accepted by the Admin API proxy connection.
proxy-ui-api.proxy-tls-cipher-suites: TLS cipher suites accepted by the Admin API proxy connection.
proxy-ui-api.key-management-api-whitelist: Comma-separated list of plain IP addresses or address ranges in CIDR notation, which are allowed to call key management endpoints using basic authentication
proxy-ui-api.regular-api-whitelist: Comma-separated list of plain IP addresses or address ranges in CIDR notation, which are allowed to call regular endpoints using api key authentication

certificate-provisioning.issuance-role-name: Vault PKI role name used when provisioning the Admin API TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.common-name: Common name set on the provisioned Admin API TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.alt-names: DNS subject alternative names included in the provisioned Admin API TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ip-subject-alt-names: IP subject alternative names included in the provisioned Admin API TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ttl: Time-to-live of the provisioned Admin API TLS certificate (e.g. 3650D).
certificate-provisioning.secret-store-pki-path: Vault PKI secrets engine mount path for Admin API TLS certificate provisioning.

proxy.admin-port: Port on which the proxy exposes its admin interface.
proxy.ssl-enabled: If true, TLS is used for connections between the service client's and service provider's security servers.
proxy.health-check-port: The TCP port where the health check service listens to requests. Setting the port to 0 disables the health check service completely.
proxy.health-check-interface: The network interface where the health check service listens to requests. Default is all available interfaces.
proxy.hsm-health-check-enabled: When enabled, the health-check endpoint also verifies HSM availability.
proxy.message-sign-digest-name: Digest algorithm used to sign X-Road messages.
proxy.verify-client-cert: When enabled, the server proxy verifies the client proxy's TLS certificate.
proxy.log-client-cert: Whether to log client certificate subject information.
proxy.enforce-client-is-cert-validity-period-c: Whether to reject a request when client information system certificate is expired or not yet valid.
proxy.server-port: Destination TCP port for outgoing queries in the service client's security server.
proxy.xroad-tls-ciphers: TLS ciphers (comma-separated list in preferred order) accepted on requests between security servers, and between operational monitoring daemon and client. (since version 6.20)
proxy.batch-signing-enabled: When enabled, multiple messages are signed in a single batch operation.
proxy.strict-identifier-checks: Configures identifier input validation (member code, subsystem code etc). Values: true - identifiers must match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9'()+,-.=?]* and non-matching values are rejected. false - identifiers are validated against the pattern, non-matching values are not rejected but a warning is logged.

client-proxy.connector-host: IP address on which the service client's security server listens for connections from client applications. The value 0.0.0.0 allows listening on all IPv4 interfaces. The value 127.0.0.1 allows listening on localhost only. NB! Changing this value could make your Security Server externally accessible and as such, a firewall rules should be implemented first to limit access to trusted hosts.
client-proxy.client-http-port: TCP port on which the service client's security server listens for HTTP requests from client applications.
client-proxy.client-https-port: TCP port on which the service client's security server listens for HTTPS requests from client applications.
client-proxy.jetty-configuration-file: Absolute filename of the Jetty configuration file for the service client's security server. For more information about configuring Jetty server, see https://www.eclipse.org/jetty/documentation/jetty-9/index.html.
client-proxy.client-connector-initial-idle-time: The initial idle time (in milliseconds) that client connections are allowed to be idle before the security server starts closing them. Value of 0 means that an infinite idle time is allowed.
client-proxy.client-httpclient-so-linger: The SO_LINGER time (in seconds) at the service consuming security server end for connections between security servers. A value larger than 0 means that upon closing a connection, the system will allow SO_LINGER seconds for the transmission and acknowledgement of all data written to the peer, at which point the socket is closed gracefully. Upon reaching the linger timeout, the socket is closed forcefully, with a TCP RST. Enabling the option with a timeout of zero does a forceful close immediately. Value of -1 disables the forceful close.
client-proxy.client-httpclient-timeout: The maximum time (SO_TIMEOUT, in milliseconds) that connections from a service consuming security server to a service providing security server are allowed to wait for a response before the consumer end httpclient gives up. Value of 0 means that an infinite wait time is allowed. This does not affect idle connections.
client-proxy.pool-total-max-connections: The total maximum number of connections that are allowed in the pool.
client-proxy.pool-total-default-max-connections-per-r: The default route specific connection maximum that is set unless a route specific connection limit is set. Due to the current implementation, this is actually the total maximum limit of connections, indepedent of what the above setting is.
client-proxy.pool-validate-connections-after-inactivi: When reusing a pooled connection to a service providing security server, check that the connection (the socket) is not half-closed if it has been idle for at least this many milliseconds. This method cannot detect half-open connections. Value of -1 disables the check.
client-proxy.client-idle-connection-monitor-interval: How often (in milliseconds) should the connection monitor go through the pooled connections to see if it can clean up any idle or expired connections. This option requires the connection monitor to be enabled to have any effect.
client-proxy.client-idle-connection-monitor-timeout: The minimum time (in milliseconds) that a pooled connection must be unused (idle) before it can be removed from the pool. Note that removal from the pool also depends on how often the connection monitor runs. This option requires the connection monitor to be enabled to have any effect.
client-proxy.client-use-idle-connection-monitor: Should the idle connection monitor be used to clean up idle and expired connections from the connection pool.
client-proxy.fastest-connecting-ssl-uri-cache-period: When a service consumer's security server finds the fastest responding service providing security server, how long the result should be kept in the TLS session cache? 0 to disable.
client-proxy.use-fastest-connecting-ssl-socket-autocl: On TLS connections between security servers, should the underlying TCP-layer connection (socket) be closed on the service consumer end when the TLS layer connection is terminated.
client-proxy.client-tls-protocols: TLS protocols (comma-separated list) enabled on the client-side interfaces (for both incoming and outgoing requests). For backward compatibility TLSv1.1 is still supported on the client-side interfaces for outgoing requests (since version 6.7)
client-proxy.client-tls-ciphers: TLS ciphers (comma-separated list) enabled on the client-side interfaces (for both incoming and outgoing requests). (since version 6.7)
client-proxy.pool-enable-connection-reuse: Allow pooled connections between security servers to be used more than once on the client side. The service provider end of the connections has to have the setting server-support-clients-pooled-connections=true for the pooling to work between a provider and consumer security servers.

server.listen-address: IP address on which the service provider's security server listens for connections from the service client's security servers. The value 0.0.0.0 allows listening on all IPv4 interfaces.
server.listen-port: TCP port on which the service provider's security server listens for connections from the service client's security server.
server.connector-initial-idle-time: The initial idle time (in milliseconds) that unauthenticated connections are allowed to be idle before the provider security server starts closing them. Value of 0 means that an infinite idle time is allowed.
server.jetty-configuration-file: Absolute filename of the Jetty configuration file for the service provider's security server. For more information about configuring Jetty server, see https://www.eclipse.org/jetty/documentation/jetty-9/index.html.
server.support-clients-pooled-connections: Whether this service providing security server supports pooled connections from the service consumer side. If set to false, connections are to be closed immediately after each message. This may be a wanted approached for security servers behind load balancers.
server.min-supported-client-version: Minimum version of the client Security Server allowed to call services on this provider. Requests from older versions are rejected. Leave empty to allow all versions.

ocsp-responder.listen-address: IP address on which the service provider's security server listens for requests for OCSP responses from the service client's security server. The service client's security server downloads OCSP responses from the service provider's security server while establishing a secure connection between the security servers. The value 0.0.0.0 allows listening on all IPv4 interfaces. Must match the value of proxy.server-listen-address.
ocsp-responder.port: TCP port on which the service provider's security server listens for requests for OCSP responses from the service client's security server. The service client's security server downloads OCSP responses from the service provider's security server while establishing a secure connection between the security servers.
ocsp-responder.client-connect-timeout: Connect timeout (in milliseconds) of the OCSP responder client. The service client's security server downloads OCSP responses from the service provider's security server while establishing a secure connection between the security servers.
ocsp-responder.client-read-timeout: Read timeout (in milliseconds) of the OCSP responder client. The service client's security server downloads OCSP responses from the service provider's security server while establishing a secure connection between the security servers.
ocsp-responder.jetty-configuration-file: Absolute filename of the Jetty configuration file for the OCSP responder of the service provider's security server. For more information about configuring Jetty server, see https://www.eclipse.org/jetty/documentation/jetty-9/index.html.

buffer.size: Maximum number of records buffered before sending to the operational monitor.
buffer.max-records-in-message: Maximum number of operational data records in a message sent by the operational monitoring buffer to the operational monitoring daemon.
buffer.sending-interval-seconds: The interval in seconds at which the operational monitoring buffer (re)tries to send records to the operational monitoring daemon. Normally, the buffer triggers the sending mechanism immediately when it receives a new record. In case of heavy load or sending failures the records are accumulating in the buffer and need periodical attention.
buffer.socket-timeout-seconds: The socket timeout (SO_TIMEOUT) of sending operational monitoring records from the operational monitoring buffer to the operational monitoring daemon in seconds.
buffer.connection-timeout-seconds: HTTP client connection timeout in seconds.

connection.host: The host address on which the operational monitoring daemon listens.
connection.port: TCP port on which the operational monitoring daemon listens.
connection.scheme: The URI scheme name of the operational monitoring daemon. Possible values are http and https.
connection.socket-timeout-seconds: HTTP client connection timeout in seconds.
connection.connection-timeout-seconds: The socket timeout (SO_TIMEOUT) of sending the operational data request to the operational monitoring daemon in seconds.
connection.xroad-tls-ciphers: TLS ciphers (comma-separated list in preferred order) accepted on requests between security servers, and between operational monitoring daemon and client. (since version 6.20)

message-log.message-body-logging: Whether message body should be logged or not. If true, the messages are logged in their original form. If false, the message body is cleared of its contents (SOAP body will have an empty child element inside it; REST message body, service path and query parameters will be omitted). In addition, the SOAP header and REST HTTP headers will only have specific set of elements logged, see Note on logged X-Road message headers . As a side effect, details such as formatting and namespace labels of the xml message can be changed and new elements may be introduced for default values in SOAP header. Removal of message body is usually done for confidentiality reasons (body contains data that we do not want to have in the logs). Note that changing the message this way prevents verifying its signature with the asicverifier tool.
message-log.max-loggable-message-body-size: Maximum loggable REST message body size
message-log.truncated-body-allowed: If the REST message body exceeds the maximum loggable body size, truncate the body in the log (true) or reject the message (false).
message-log.hash-algo-id: The algorithm identifier used for hashing in the message log. Possible values are - SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512.
message-log.timestamping-prioritization-strategy: Timestamping prioritization strategy, that determines what timestamping services and in what order are used to timestamp. Possible values are: ONLY_FREE - Only free timestamping services are used. ONLY_PAID - only paid timestamping services are used. FREE_FIRST - free timestamping services are used first, then if no successful responses, then paid services are used next, finally timestamping services whose cost type is undefined are used last. PAID_FIRST - paid timestamping services are used first, then if no successful responses, then free services are used next, finally timestamping services whose cost type is undefined are used last. NONE - no new ordering nor filtering is added (same as before adding cost type to timestamping services.)
message-log.enabled-body-logging-local-producer-subs: Subsystem-specific overrides for message body logging when message-body-logging = false. This parameter defines logging for local producer subsystems, that is, our subsystems that produce some service which external clients use. Comma-separated list of client identifiers for which message body logging is enabled. For example FI/ORG/1710128-9/SUBSYSTEM_A1, FI/ORG/1710128-9/SUBSYSTEM_A2, where - FI = x-road instance, ORG = member class, 1710128-9 = member code, SUBSYSTEM_A1 = subsystem code. This parameter can only be used on subsystem-level, it is not possible to configure message body logging per member. If a subsystem has forward slashes “/” in for example subsystem code, those subsystems can’t be configured with this parameter.
message-log.enabled-body-logging-remote-producer-sub: Subsystem-specific overrides for remote producer subsystems, that is, remote subsystems that produce services which we use. Parameter is used when message-body-logging = false.
message-log.disabled-body-logging-local-producer-sub: Same as enabled-body-logging-local-producer-subsystems, but this parameter is used when message-body-logging = true.
message-log.disabled-body-logging-remote-producer-su: Same as enabled-body-logging-remote-producer-subsystems, but this parameter is used when message-body-logging = true.

timestamper.client-connect-timeout: The timestamper client connect timeout in milliseconds. A timeout of zero is interpreted as an infinite timeout.
timestamper.client-read-timeout: The timestamper client read timeout in milliseconds. A timeout of zero is interpreted as an infinite timeout.
timestamper.timestamp-immediately: If true, the time-stamp is created synchronously for each request message. This is a security policy requirement to guarantee the time-stamp at the time of logging the message.
timestamper.records-limit: Maximum number of message records to time-stamp in one batch. If the number of message records in a single batch exceeds 70 % of timestamp-records-limit value, a warning is logged in proxy.log.
timestamper.retry-delay: Time-stamp retry delay in seconds when batch time-stamping fails. After failing to batch time-stamp, the timestamper waits for the time period defined by "timestamp-retry-delay" before trying again. This is repeated until fetching a time-stamp succeeds. After successfully fetching a time-stamp, the timestamper returns to normal time-stamping schedule. If the value of "timestamp-retry-delay" is higher than the value of the central server system parameter "timeStampingIntervalSeconds", the value of "timeStampingIntervalSeconds" is used. If the value of "timestamp-retry-delay" is zero, the value of "timeStampingIntervalSeconds" is used.
timestamper.acceptable-timestamp-failure-period: Defines the time period (in seconds) for how long is time-stamping allowed to fail (for whatever reasons) before the message log stops accepting any more messages (and consequently the security server stops accepting requests). Set to 0 to disable this check. The value of this parameter should not be lower than the value of the central server system parameter timeStampingIntervalSeconds.

certificate-provisioning.issuance-role-name: Vault PKI role name used when provisioning the proxy TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.common-name: Common name set on the provisioned proxy TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.alt-names: DNS subject alternative names included in the provisioned proxy TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ip-subject-alt-names: IP subject alternative names included in the provisioned proxy TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ttl: Time-to-live of the provisioned proxy TLS certificate (e.g. 3650D).
certificate-provisioning.secret-store-pki-path: Vault PKI secrets engine mount path for proxy TLS certificate provisioning.

rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the proxy gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: The (localhost) port where the proxy gRPC server binds to. Used for communicating with xroad-signer and xroad-monitor.

signer.selfsigned-cert-digest-algorithm: Digest algorithm used when creating self-signed certificates.
signer.csr-signature-digest-algorithm: Certificate Signing Request signature digest algorithm. Possible values are - SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512.
signer.enforce-token-pin-policy: Controls enforcing the token pin policy. When set to true, software token pin is required to be at least 10 ASCII characters from at least tree character classes (lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, special characters). (since version 6.7.7)
signer.ocsp-response-retrieval-active: This property is used as an override to deactivate periodic OCSP-response retrieval for components that don't need that functionality, but still use signer. Values: false - OCSP-response retrieval jobs are never scheduled. true - periodic OCSP-response retrieval is active based on ocspFetchInterval. Note that if the entire property is missing, it is interpreted as true. This property is delivered as an override and only for the components where the OCSP-response retrieval jobs need to be deactivated. The property is missing for components that require OCSP-response retrieval to be activated.
signer.ocsp-retry-delay: OCSP retry delay for signer when fetching OCSP responses fail. After failing to fetch OCSP responses signer waits for the time period defined by "ocsp-retry-delay" before trying again. This is repeated until fetching OCSP responses succeeds. After successfully fetching OCSP responses signer returns to normal OCSP refresh schedule defined by "ocspFetchInterval". If the value of "ocsp-retry-delay" is higher than "ocspFetchInterval", the value of "ocspFetchInterval" is used as OCSP retry delay.
signer.ocsp-cache-path: Absolute path to the directory where the cached OCSP responses are stored.
signer.ocsp-prioritization-strategy: OCSP prioritization strategy, that determines what OCSP responders and in what order are used to get OCSP responses. Possible values are: ONLY_FREE - Only free OCSP responders are used. ONLY_PAID - only paid OCSP responders are used. FREE_FIRST - free OCSP responders are used first, then if no successful responses, then paid responders are used next, finally OCSP responders whose cost type is undefined are used last. PAID_FIRST - paid OCSP responders are used first, then if no successful responses, then free responders are used next, finally OCSP responders whose cost type is undefined are used last. NONE - no new ordering nor filtering is added (same as before adding cost type to OCSP endpoints.)
signer.module-manager-update-interval: HSM module manager update interval in seconds.
signer.soft-token-rsa-sign-mechanism: PKCS#11 mechanism used for RSA signing on the software token.
signer.soft-token-ec-sign-mechanism: PKCS#11 mechanism used for EC signing on the software token.
signer.soft-token-pin-keystore-algorithm: Key algorithm used for creating PIN keystore for software token. Possible values are RSA and EC. (since version 7.6)
signer.key-length: Key length for generating authentication and signing keys (since version 6.7)
signer.key-named-curve: Named curve for generating authentication and signing keys in case EC algorithms are used (since version 7.6)

autologin.enabled: Enable automatic token login on startup.

retry.retry-delay: Initial delay between autologin retry attempts (e.g. 3S).
retry.retry-exponential-backoff-multiplier: Multiplier applied to the retry delay on each subsequent autologin attempt.
retry.retry-max-attempts: Maximum number of autologin retry attempts.
retry.retry-timeout: Total time limit for all autologin retry attempts (e.g. 60S).

hwtoken.session-pool-enabled: Enable pooling of PKCS#11 sessions for the hardware token.
hwtoken.session-pool-max-total: Maximum total PKCS#11 sessions in the hardware token session pool.
hwtoken.session-pool-min-idle: Minimum number of idle PKCS#11 sessions kept in the hardware token pool.
hwtoken.session-pool-max-idle: Maximum number of idle PKCS#11 sessions kept in the hardware token pool.
hwtoken.session-acquire-timeout: Maximum time to wait when acquiring a PKCS#11 session from the pool (e.g. 15S).

rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the Signer gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: Port on which the Signer gRPC server listens.

pin-hasher.iterations: Argon2 iteration count used when hashing token PINs.
pin-hasher.memory-kb: Argon2 memory cost in kilobytes used when hashing token PINs.
pin-hasher.parallelism: Argon2 parallelism degree used when hashing token PINs.
pin-hasher.hash-length: Output hash length in bytes used when hashing token PINs.

configuration-client.allowed-federations: A comma-separated list of case-insensitive X-Road instances that fetching configuration anchors is allowed for. This enables federation with the listed instances if the X-Road instance is already federated at the central server level . Special value none, if present, disables all federation (the default value), while all allows all federations if none is not present. Example: allowed-federations=ee,sv allows federation with example instances EE and Sv while allowed-federations=all,none disables federation. X-Road services xroad-confclient and xroad-proxy need to be restarted (in that order) for the setting change to take effect.
configuration-client.global-conf-hostname-verification: It is possible to disable the hostname verification. Does the hostname specified in the URL match the hostname specified in the Common Name (CN) of the Central Server’s TLS certificate. Should be true in production environment
configuration-client.global-conf-tls-cert-verification: It is possible to disable the verification of the global configuration download TLS certificate. Should be true in production environment
configuration-client.downloader-connect-timeout: Maximum time in milliseconds the Global configuration downloader waits to connect to the remote server.
configuration-client.downloader-read-timeout: Maximum time in milliseconds the Global configuration downloader waits to read data from the remote server after the connection is established.
configuration-client.global-conf-dir: File system path where the downloaded global configuration is stored.
configuration-client.update-interval: Global configuration download interval in seconds.
configuration-client.configuration-anchor-file: Absolute file name of the configuration anchor that is used to download global configuration.
configuration-client.configuration-anchor-storage: Storage backend for the configuration anchor (DB or FILE).

rpc.enabled: Enable the configuration client gRPC server.
rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the configuration client gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: Port on which the configuration client gRPC server listens.

env-monitor.certificate-info-sensor-interval: Interval of certificate information sensor in seconds. How often certificate data is collected. The first collection is always done after a delay of 10 seconds.
env-monitor.disk-space-sensor-interval: Interval of disk space sensor in seconds. How often disk space data is collected.
env-monitor.exec-listing-sensor-interval: Interval of exec listing sensor in seconds. How often sensor data using external command are collected.
env-monitor.system-metrics-sensor-interval: Interval of systems metrics sensor in seconds. How often system metrics data is collected.
env-monitor.limit-remote-data-set: On/Off switch for filtering out optional monitoring data. With flag set to true, only security server owner can request and get full data set.

rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the env-monitor gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: Port on which the env-monitor gRPC server listens.

anti-dos.max-parallel-connections: Maximum number of parallel connections for AntiDOS.
anti-dos.min-free-file-handles: Minimum amount of free file handles in the system for accepting new connections. At least one free file handle must be available to accept a new connection.
anti-dos.max-cpu-load: Maximum allowed CPU load for accepting new connections. If set to > 1.0, then CPU load is not checked.
anti-dos.max-heap-usage: Specifies the maximum allowed Java heap usage when accepting new connections. If set to > 1.0, then heap usage is not checked.
anti-dos.enabled: Flag for enabling or disabling the AntiDOS system.

common-rpc.use-tls: When enabled, mutual TLS is used for all gRPC communication between the Security Server internal services.

certificate-provisioning.refresh-interval: How often services check whether their gRPC TLS certificate needs to be renewed (e.g. 5H).
certificate-provisioning.retry-delay: Initial delay between gRPC TLS certificate provisioning retry attempts (e.g. 5S).
certificate-provisioning.retry-exponential-backoff-multiplier: Multiplier applied to the retry delay on each subsequent certificate provisioning attempt.
certificate-provisioning.retry-max-attempts: Maximum number of gRPC TLS certificate provisioning retry attempts.
certificate-provisioning.retry-timeout: Total time limit for all gRPC TLS certificate provisioning retry attempts (e.g. 60S).

proxy.host: Hostname used to connect to the proxy gRPC server.
proxy.port: Port used to connect to the proxy gRPC server.
proxy.deadline-after: Milliseconds before a gRPC call to the proxy times out.

configuration-client.host: Hostname used to connect to the configuration client gRPC server.
configuration-client.port: Port used to connect to the configuration client gRPC server.
configuration-client.deadline-after: Milliseconds before a gRPC call to the configuration client times out.

env-monitor.host: Hostname used to connect to the env-monitor gRPC server.
env-monitor.port: Port used to connect to the env-monitor gRPC server.
env-monitor.deadline-after: Milliseconds before a gRPC call to the env-monitor times out.

auxiliary-service.host: Hostname used to connect to the auxiliary service gRPC server.
auxiliary-service.port: Port used to connect to the auxiliary service gRPC server.
auxiliary-service.deadline-after: Milliseconds before a gRPC call to the auxiliary service times out.

op-monitor.host: Hostname used to connect to the operational monitoring daemon gRPC server.
op-monitor.port: Port used to connect to the operational monitoring daemon gRPC server.
op-monitor.deadline-after: Milliseconds before a gRPC call to the operational monitoring daemon times out.

common-global-conf.source: Source backend for global configuration. Possible values: FILESYSTEM (read from local files) or DB (read from database).
common-global-conf.refresh-rate: How often the shared global configuration cache is refreshed from the configured source (e.g. 60S).
common-global-conf.configuration-path: File system path where the global configuration files are stored.

common-server-conf.cache-period: How long (in seconds) server configuration entries are cached before being re-read.
common-server-conf.client-cache-size: Maximum number of entries in the server configuration client cache.
common-server-conf.service-cache-size: Maximum number of entries in the server configuration service cache.
common-server-conf.service-endpoints-cache-size: Maximum number of service endpoint entries kept in the server configuration cache.
common-server-conf.acl-cache-size: Maximum number of entries in the server configuration access control list (ACL) cache.

common-ocsp-verifier.cache-period: How long (in seconds) OCSP verification results are cached before being re-checked.

backup.location: File system directory where backup archives are stored.
backup.valid-filename-pattern: Regular expression that valid backup filenames must match.
backup.autobackup-cron-expression: Cron expression controlling when automatic backups are created.
backup.autobackup-script-path: Path to the script executed when an automatic backup runs.
backup.autobackup-delete-old-backups-cron: Cron expression controlling when old automatic backups are deleted.
backup.script-path: Path to the manual backup script.
backup.restore-script-path: Path to the backup restore script.
backup.generate-gpg-keypair-path: Path to the script that generates a GPG key pair for backup encryption.
backup.create-backup-metadata-path: Path to the script that parses an uploaded backup's tar label and writes its ".metadata" file.
backup.backup-format-version-file-path: Path to the file containing the current backup format version, used to determine backup compatibility.
backup.gpgkeys-home: Directory used as the GNUPGHOME for backup GPG operations.
backup.encryption-enabled: When enabled, backup archives are encrypted with GPG.
backup.encryption-keyids: Comma-separated GPG key IDs used to encrypt backup archives.

rpc.enabled: Enable the auxiliary service gRPC server.
rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the auxiliary service gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: Port on which the auxiliary service gRPC server listens.

kubernetes.service-host: Kubernetes API server hostname for readiness checks (leave empty to disable).
kubernetes.service-port: Kubernetes API server port for readiness checks.
kubernetes.token-path: File system path to the Kubernetes service account token used for readiness checks.
kubernetes.ca-cert-path: File system path to the Kubernetes CA certificate used for readiness checks.
kubernetes.connect-timeout-ms: Milliseconds to wait when connecting to the Kubernetes API for readiness checks.
kubernetes.read-timeout-ms: Milliseconds to wait when reading a response from the Kubernetes API for readiness checks.

message-log.archive-cron: Cron expression controlling when message log archiving runs.
message-log.clean-cron: Cron expression controlling when old message log records are cleaned up.
message-log.command-path: Path to the message log archiver executable.

op-monitor.listen-address: IP address on which the operational monitoring daemon listens.
op-monitor.port: TCP port on which the operational monitoring daemon listens.
op-monitor.scheme: URI scheme of the operational monitoring daemon. Possible values are http and https.
op-monitor.xroad-tls-ciphers: TLS ciphers (comma-separated list in preferred order) accepted on connections to the operational monitoring daemon.
op-monitor.keep-records-for-days: Number of days to retain operational monitoring records before they are deleted.
op-monitor.clean-interval: Cron expression controlling when old operational monitoring records are cleaned up.
op-monitor.max-records-in-payload: Maximum number of operational monitoring records returned in a single response payload.
op-monitor.records-available-timestamp-offset-secon: Offset in seconds subtracted from the current time when determining the upper bound for available records.
op-monitor.health-statistics-period-seconds: Period in seconds over which health statistics are aggregated.

rpc.enabled: Enable the operational monitoring daemon gRPC server.
rpc.listen-address: IP address on which the operational monitoring daemon gRPC server listens.
rpc.port: Port on which the operational monitoring daemon gRPC server listens.

certificate-provisioning.issuance-role-name: Vault PKI role name used when provisioning the operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.common-name: Common name set on the provisioned operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.alt-names: DNS subject alternative names included in the provisioned operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ip-subject-alt-names: IP subject alternative names included in the provisioned operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate.
certificate-provisioning.ttl: Time-to-live of the provisioned operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate (e.g. 3650D).
certificate-provisioning.secret-store-pki-path: Vault PKI secrets engine mount path for operational monitoring daemon TLS certificate provisioning.

tls.client-certificate-refresh-interval: Interval at which the operational monitoring daemon refreshes its client TLS certificate (e.g. 0S to disable).

message-log-archiver.clean-transaction-batch-size: Maximum number of message log records removed per database transaction during clean-up.
message-log-archiver.clean-keep-records-for: Number of days to retain archived message log records before they are deleted.
message-log-archiver.max-filesize: Maximum size in bytes of a single message log archive file.
message-log-archiver.transaction-batch-size: Number of message log records processed in a single archiving transaction batch.
message-log-archiver.archive-path: Absolute path to the directory where archived message log files are stored.
message-log-archiver.archive-transfer-command: Shell command executed after each archiving run to transfer archive files (e.g. to remote storage). Leave empty to disable.
message-log-archiver.hash-algo-id: The algorithm identifier used for hashing in the message log archive. Possible values are SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512.

archive.encryption-enabled: When enabled, message log archive files are encrypted using OpenPGP (GnuPG).
archive.default-key-id: Default OpenPGP key ID used to encrypt message log archive files when no member-specific key is configured.
archive.grouping-strategy: Strategy for grouping records into archive files. Possible values: NONE (no grouping), MEMBER (group by member), SUBSYSTEM (group by subsystem).

db.encryption-enabled: When enabled, message bodies are stored in the database in encrypted form.
db.key-id: Identifier of the encryption key used for database-level message log encryption.

memory.threshold-percent: Maximum allowed percentage (0-100) of heap memory usage before the liveness health check reports DOWN. Unset means the check never fails; containers default to 95.

common.temp-files-path: Absolute path to the directory where temporary files are stored.
